Exo.11.7.kjv: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.

Exo.12.13.bsb: The blood on the houses where you are staying will be a sign; when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No plague will fall on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Exo.12.13.kjv: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

Exo.12.17.bsb: So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
Exo.12.17.kjv: And ye shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day in your generations by an ordinance for ever.

Exo.12.23.bsb: When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway; so He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
Exo.12.23.kjv: For the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.

Exo.14.29.bsb: But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
Exo.14.29.kjv: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

Exo.14.30.bsb: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore.
Exo.14.30.kjv: Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.

Exo.16.15.bsb: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
Exo.16.15.kjv: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.

Exo.23.21.bsb: Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.
Exo.23.21.kjv: Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.

Exo.23.22.bsb: But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
Exo.23.22.kjv: But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.

Exo.23.24.bsb: You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
Exo.23.24.kjv: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.

Exo.23.25.bsb: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.
Exo.23.25.kjv: And ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.

Exo.23.26.bsb: No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
Exo.23.26.kjv: There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I will fulfil.

Exo.23.27.bsb: I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
Exo.23.27.kjv: I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.

Exo.23.28.bsb: I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
Exo.23.28.kjv: And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.

Exo.23.29.bsb: I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
Exo.23.29.kjv: I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee.

Exo.23.30.bsb: Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
Exo.23.30.kjv: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.

Exo.23.31.bsb: And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
Exo.23.31.kjv: And I will set thy bounds from the Red sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand; and thou shalt drive them out before thee.

Exo.34.24.bsb: For I will drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
Exo.34.24.kjv: For I will cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the Lord thy God thrice in the year.

Exo.2.1.bsb: Now a man of the house of Levi married a Levite woman,
Exo.2.1.kjv: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

Exo.2.3.bsb: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
Exo.2.3.kjv: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

Exo.2.4.bsb: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
Exo.2.4.kjv: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

Exo.1.9.bsb: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.
Exo.1.9.kjv: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:

Exo.1.10.bsb: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more; and if a war breaks out, they may join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country.”
Exo.1.10.kjv: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.

Exo.1.11.bsb: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
Exo.1.11.kjv: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

Exo.1.12.bsb: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
Exo.1.12.kjv: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.

Exo.9.4.bsb: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’”
Exo.9.4.kjv: And the Lord shall sever between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: and there shall nothing die of all that is the children’s of Israel.

Exo.9.5.bsb: The LORD set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
Exo.9.5.kjv: And the Lord appointed a set time, saying, To morrow the Lord shall do this thing in the land.

Exo.9.6.bsb: And the next day the LORD did just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
Exo.9.6.kjv: And the Lord did that thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt died: but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.

Exo.9.7.bsb: Pharaoh sent officials and found that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go.
Exo.9.7.kjv: And Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the people go.

Exo.10.21.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt—a palpable darkness.”
Exo.10.21.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.

Exo.10.22.bsb: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
Exo.10.22.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:

Exo.10.23.bsb: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place. Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
Exo.10.23.kjv: They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

Exo.13.3.bsb: So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.
Exo.13.3.kjv: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

Exo.13.17.bsb: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
Exo.13.17.kjv: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

Exo.13.18.bsb: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
Exo.13.18.kjv: But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

Exo.13.19.bsb: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”
Exo.13.19.kjv: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

Exo.15.26.bsb: saying, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and keep all His statutes, then I will not bring on you any of the diseases I inflicted on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
Exo.15.26.kjv: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.

Exo.11.3.bsb: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.
Exo.11.3.kjv: And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.

Exo.14.21.bsb: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
Exo.14.21.kjv: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

Exo.14.25.bsb: He caused their chariot wheels to wobble, so that they had difficulty driving. “Let us flee from the Israelites,” said the Egyptians, “for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
Exo.14.25.kjv: And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.

Exo.14.26.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”
Exo.14.26.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.

Exo.14.27.bsb: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea returned to its normal state. As the Egyptians were retreating, the LORD swept them into the sea.
Exo.14.27.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

Exo.14.28.bsb: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
Exo.14.28.kjv: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

Exo.15.25.bsb: And Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a log. And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened. There the LORD made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them,
Exo.15.25.kjv: And he cried unto the Lord; and the Lord shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them,

Exo.16.13.bsb: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
Exo.16.13.kjv: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.

Exo.16.14.bsb: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
Exo.16.14.kjv: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground.

Exo.5.20.bsb: When they left Pharaoh, they confronted Moses and Aaron, who stood waiting to meet them.
Exo.5.20.kjv: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:

Exo.5.21.bsb: “May the LORD look upon you and judge you,” the foremen said, “for you have made us a stench before Pharaoh and his officials; you have placed in their hand a sword to kill us!”
Exo.5.21.kjv: And they said unto them, The Lord look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.

Exo.5.22.bsb: So Moses returned to the LORD and asked, “Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?
Exo.5.22.kjv: And Moses returned unto the Lord, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?

Exo.5.23.bsb: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and You have not delivered Your people in any way.”
Exo.5.23.kjv: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.

Exo.9.29.bsb: Moses said to him, “When I have left the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
Exo.9.29.kjv: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands unto the Lord; and the thunder shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail; that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord’s.

Exo.18.13.bsb: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
Exo.18.13.kjv: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood by Moses from the morning unto the evening.

Exo.18.14.bsb: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
Exo.18.14.kjv: And when Moses’ father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even?

Exo.18.15.bsb: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
Exo.18.15.kjv: And Moses said unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to enquire of God:

Exo.18.16.bsb: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
Exo.18.16.kjv: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.

Exo.18.17.bsb: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
Exo.18.17.kjv: And Moses’ father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.

Exo.18.18.bsb: Surely you and these people with you will wear yourselves out, because the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
Exo.18.18.kjv: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

Exo.18.19.bsb: Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
Exo.18.19.kjv: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God:

Exo.18.20.bsb: Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the way to live and the work they must do.
Exo.18.20.kjv: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.

Exo.18.21.bsb: Furthermore, select capable men from among the people—God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
Exo.18.21.kjv: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

Exo.18.22.bsb: Have these men judge the people at all times. Then they can bring you any major issue, but all minor cases they can judge on their own, so that your load may be lightened as they share it with you.
Exo.18.22.kjv: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.

Exo.18.23.bsb: If you follow this advice and God so directs you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people can go home in peace.”
Exo.18.23.kjv: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.

Exo.18.24.bsb: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
Exo.18.24.kjv: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.

Exo.18.25.bsb: So Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
Exo.18.25.kjv: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

Exo.18.26.bsb: And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
Exo.18.26.kjv: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

Exo.19.7.bsb: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
Exo.19.7.kjv: And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and laid before their faces all these words which the Lord commanded him.

Exo.19.8.bsb: And all the people answered together, “We will do everything that the LORD has spoken.” So Moses brought their words back to the LORD.
Exo.19.8.kjv: And all the people answered together, and said, All that the Lord hath spoken we will do. And Moses returned the words of the people unto the Lord.

Exo.24.3.bsb: When Moses came and told the people all the words and ordinances of the LORD, they all responded with one voice: “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.”
Exo.24.3.kjv: And Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord, and all the judgments: and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do.

Exo.3.16.bsb: Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—has appeared to me and said: I have surely attended to you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.
Exo.3.16.kjv: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:

Exo.3.18.bsb: The elders of Israel will listen to what you say, and you must go with them to the king of Egypt and tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’
Exo.3.18.kjv: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, The Lord God of the Hebrews hath met with us: and now let us go, we beseech thee, three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God.

Exo.4.29.bsb: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites,
Exo.4.29.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel:

Exo.4.30.bsb: and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people,
Exo.4.30.kjv: And Aaron spake all the words which the Lord had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.

Exo.12.21.bsb: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and told them, “Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
Exo.12.21.kjv: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover.

Exo.18.12.bsb: Then Moses’ father-in-law Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.
Exo.18.12.kjv: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father in law before God.

Exo.24.1.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders—and you are to worship at a distance.
Exo.24.1.kjv: And he said unto Moses, Come up unto the Lord, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship ye afar off.

Exo.24.14.bsb: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”
Exo.24.14.kjv: And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until we come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: if any man have any matters to do, let him come unto them.

Exo.10.1.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,
Exo.10.1.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him:

Exo.10.7.bsb: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?”
Exo.10.7.kjv: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?

Exo.12.30.bsb: During the night Pharaoh got up—he and all his officials and all the Egyptians—and there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead.
Exo.12.30.kjv: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

Exo.14.5.bsb: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have released Israel from serving us.”
Exo.14.5.kjv: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said, Why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us?

Exo.19.3.bsb: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, “This is what you are to tell the house of Jacob and explain to the sons of Israel:
Exo.19.3.kjv: And Moses went up unto God, and the Lord called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel;

Exo.31.3.bsb: And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
Exo.31.3.kjv: And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,

Exo.35.31.bsb: And He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
Exo.35.31.kjv: And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship;

Exo.32.6.bsb: So the next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.
Exo.32.6.kjv: And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

Exo.32.25.bsb: Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
Exo.32.25.kjv: And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)

Exo.32.18.bsb: But Moses replied: “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!”
Exo.32.18.kjv: And he said, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome: but the noise of them that sing do I hear.

Exo.32.19.bsb: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.
Exo.32.19.kjv: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.

Exo.12.12.bsb: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
Exo.12.12.kjv: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord.

Exo.32.4.bsb: He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf. And they said, “These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
Exo.32.4.kjv: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

Exo.20.4.bsb: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
Exo.20.4.kjv: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

Exo.20.23.bsb: You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.
Exo.20.23.kjv: Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold.

Exo.23.13.bsb: Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.
Exo.23.13.kjv: And in all things that I have said unto you be circumspect: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.

Exo.34.17.bsb: You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.
Exo.34.17.kjv: Thou shalt make thee no molten gods.

Exo.32.20.bsb: Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the powder over the face of the water. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it.
Exo.32.20.kjv: And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.

Exo.16.32.bsb: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
Exo.16.32.kjv: And Moses said, This is the thing which the Lord commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.

Exo.10.2.bsb: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”
Exo.10.2.kjv: And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know how that I am the Lord.

Exo.12.26.bsb: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’
Exo.12.26.kjv: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?

Exo.12.27.bsb: you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
Exo.12.27.kjv: That ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.

Exo.13.11.bsb: And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,
Exo.13.11.kjv: And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,

Exo.13.12.bsb: you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
Exo.13.12.kjv: That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.

Exo.13.13.bsb: You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.
Exo.13.13.kjv: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

Exo.34.13.bsb: Rather, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.
Exo.34.13.kjv: But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves:

Exo.7.14.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
Exo.7.14.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Pharaoh’s heart is hardened, he refuseth to let the people go.

Exo.32.35.bsb: And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they had done with the calf that Aaron had made.
Exo.32.35.kjv: And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

Exo.14.17.bsb: And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. Then I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army and chariots and horsemen.
Exo.14.17.kjv: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall follow them: and I will get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

Exo.14.18.bsb: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”
Exo.14.18.kjv: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I have gotten me honour upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

Exo.14.31.bsb: When Israel saw the great power that the LORD had exercised over the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and believed in Him and in His servant Moses.
Exo.14.31.kjv: And Israel saw that great work which the Lord did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses.

Exo.32.26.bsb: So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” And all the Levites gathered around him.
Exo.32.26.kjv: Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

Exo.32.27.bsb: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you men is to fasten his sword to his side, go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”
Exo.32.27.kjv: And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.

Exo.32.28.bsb: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.
Exo.32.28.kjv: And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.

Exo.28.1.bsb: “Next, have your brother Aaron brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, to serve Me as priests.
Exo.28.1.kjv: And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

Exo.13.2.bsb: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”
Exo.13.2.kjv: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.

Exo.22.29.bsb: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
Exo.22.29.kjv: Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.

Exo.22.30.bsb: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
Exo.22.30.kjv: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.

Exo.23.15.bsb: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.
Exo.23.15.kjv: Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Abib; for in it thou camest out from Egypt: and none shall appear before me empty:)

Exo.25.1.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses,
Exo.25.1.kjv: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Exo.25.2.bsb: “Tell the Israelites to bring Me an offering. You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him.
Exo.25.2.kjv: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me an offering: of every man that giveth it willingly with his heart ye shall take my offering.

Exo.25.3.bsb: This is the offering you are to accept from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
Exo.25.3.kjv: And this is the offering which ye shall take of them; gold, and silver, and brass,

Exo.25.4.bsb: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
Exo.25.4.kjv: And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,

Exo.25.5.bsb: ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
Exo.25.5.kjv: And rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim wood,

Exo.25.6.bsb: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
Exo.25.6.kjv: Oil for the light, spices for anointing oil, and for sweet incense,

Exo.25.7.bsb: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.
Exo.25.7.kjv: Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.

Exo.34.20.bsb: You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb; but if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
Exo.34.20.kjv: But the firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb: and if thou redeem him not, then shalt thou break his neck. All the firstborn of thy sons thou shalt redeem. And none shall appear before me empty.

Exo.35.4.bsb: Moses also told the whole congregation of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
Exo.35.4.kjv: And Moses spake unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the Lord commanded, saying,

Exo.35.5.bsb: Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring an offering to the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze;
Exo.35.5.kjv: Take ye from among you an offering unto the Lord: whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it, an offering of the Lord; gold, and silver, and brass,

Exo.35.6.bsb: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
Exo.35.6.kjv: And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,

Exo.35.7.bsb: ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
Exo.35.7.kjv: And rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim wood,

Exo.35.8.bsb: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
Exo.35.8.kjv: And oil for the light, and spices for anointing oil, and for the sweet incense,

Exo.35.9.bsb: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.
Exo.35.9.kjv: And onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod, and for the breastplate.

Exo.35.10.bsb: Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:
Exo.35.10.kjv: And every wise hearted among you shall come, and make all that the Lord hath commanded;

Exo.35.11.bsb: the tabernacle with its tent and covering, its clasps and frames, its crossbars, posts, and bases;
Exo.35.11.kjv: The tabernacle, his tent, and his covering, his taches, and his boards, his bars, his pillars, and his sockets,

Exo.35.12.bsb: the ark with its poles and mercy seat, and the veil to shield it;
Exo.35.12.kjv: The ark, and the staves thereof, with the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering,

Exo.35.13.bsb: the table with its poles, all its utensils, and the Bread of the Presence;
Exo.35.13.kjv: The table, and his staves, and all his vessels, and the shewbread,

Exo.35.14.bsb: the lampstand for light with its accessories and lamps and oil for the light;
Exo.35.14.kjv: The candlestick also for the light, and his furniture, and his lamps, with the oil for the light,

Exo.35.15.bsb: the altar of incense with its poles; the anointing oil and fragrant incense; the curtain for the doorway at the entrance to the tabernacle;
Exo.35.15.kjv: And the incense altar, and his staves, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the hanging for the door at the entering in of the tabernacle,

Exo.35.16.bsb: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
Exo.35.16.kjv: The altar of burnt offering, with his brasen grate, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver and his foot,

Exo.35.17.bsb: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the gate of the courtyard;
Exo.35.17.kjv: The hangings of the court, his pillars, and their sockets, and the hanging for the door of the court,

Exo.35.18.bsb: the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, along with their ropes;
Exo.35.18.kjv: The pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords,

Exo.35.19.bsb: and the woven garments for ministering in the holy place—both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.”
Exo.35.19.kjv: The cloths of service, to do service in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.

Exo.35.20.bsb: Then the whole congregation of Israel withdrew from the presence of Moses.
Exo.35.20.kjv: And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.

Exo.35.21.bsb: And everyone whose heart stirred him and whose spirit prompted him came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work on the Tent of Meeting, for all its services, and for the holy garments.
Exo.35.21.kjv: And they came, every one whose heart stirred him up, and every one whom his spirit made willing, and they brought the Lord’s offering to the work of the tabernacle of the congregation, and for all his service, and for the holy garments.

Exo.35.22.bsb: So all who had willing hearts, both men and women, came and brought brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry. And they all presented their gold as a wave offering to the LORD.
Exo.35.22.kjv: And they came, both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, and brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold: and every man that offered offered an offering of gold unto the Lord.

Exo.35.23.bsb: Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, or articles of fine leather, brought them.
Exo.35.23.kjv: And every man, with whom was found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, and red skins of rams, and badgers’ skins, brought them.

Exo.35.24.bsb: And all who could present an offering of silver or bronze brought it as a contribution to the LORD. Also, everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the service brought it.
Exo.35.24.kjv: Every one that did offer an offering of silver and brass brought the Lord’s offering: and every man, with whom was found shittim wood for any work of the service, brought it.

Exo.35.25.bsb: Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen.
Exo.35.25.kjv: And all the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands, and brought that which they had spun, both of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine linen.

Exo.35.26.bsb: And all the skilled women whose hearts were stirred spun the goat hair.
Exo.35.26.kjv: And all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats’ hair.

Exo.35.27.bsb: The leaders brought onyx stones and gemstones to mount on the ephod and breastpiece,
Exo.35.27.kjv: And the rulers brought onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate;

Exo.35.28.bsb: as well as spices and olive oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
Exo.35.28.kjv: And spice, and oil for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.

Exo.35.29.bsb: So all the men and women of the Israelites whose hearts prompted them brought a freewill offering to the LORD for all the work that the LORD through Moses had commanded them to do.
Exo.35.29.kjv: The children of Israel brought a willing offering unto the Lord, every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all manner of work, which the Lord had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses.

Exo.36.3.bsb: They received from Moses all the contributions that the Israelites had brought to carry out the service of constructing the sanctuary. Meanwhile, the people continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning,
Exo.36.3.kjv: And they received of Moses all the offering, which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to make it withal. And they brought yet unto him free offerings every morning.

Exo.36.4.bsb: so that all the skilled craftsmen who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left their work
Exo.36.4.kjv: And all the wise men, that wrought all the work of the sanctuary, came every man from his work which they made;

Exo.36.5.bsb: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.”
Exo.36.5.kjv: And they spake unto Moses, saying, The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work, which the Lord commanded to make.

Exo.36.6.bsb: After Moses had given an order, they sent a proclamation throughout the camp: “No man or woman should make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing more,
Exo.36.6.kjv: And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing.

Exo.36.7.bsb: since what they already had was more than enough to perform all the work.
Exo.36.7.kjv: For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.

Exo.34.16.bsb: And when you take some of their daughters as brides for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and cause your sons to do the same.
Exo.34.16.kjv: And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.

Exo.28.4.bsb: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests.
Exo.28.4.kjv: And these are the garments which they shall make; a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

Exo.28.36.bsb: You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
Exo.28.36.kjv: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.

Exo.28.37.bsb: Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.
Exo.28.37.kjv: And thou shalt put it on a blue lace, that it may be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.

Exo.28.38.bsb: And it will be worn on Aaron’s forehead, so that he may bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD.
Exo.28.38.kjv: And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the Lord.

Exo.28.39.bsb: You are to weave the tunic with fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.
Exo.28.39.kjv: And thou shalt embroider the coat of fine linen, and thou shalt make the mitre of fine linen, and thou shalt make the girdle of needlework.

Exo.39.29.bsb: and the sash of finely spun linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Exo.39.29.kjv: And a girdle of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, of needlework; as the Lord commanded Moses.

Exo.39.31.bsb: Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Exo.39.31.kjv: And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten it on high upon the mitre; as the Lord commanded Moses.

Exo.33.4.bsb: When the people heard this bad news, they went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.
Exo.33.4.kjv: And when the people heard these evil tidings, they mourned: and no man did put on him his ornaments.

Exo.33.6.bsb: So the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.
Exo.33.6.kjv: And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments by the mount Horeb.

Exo.21.18.bsb: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
Exo.21.18.kjv: And if men strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keepeth his bed:

Exo.21.19.bsb: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
Exo.21.19.kjv: If he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.

Exo.21.20.bsb: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
Exo.21.20.kjv: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall be surely punished.

Exo.20.16.bsb: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
Exo.20.16.kjv: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

Exo.20.10.bsb: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.
Exo.20.10.kjv: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

Exo.30.15.bsb: In making the offering to the LORD to atone for your lives, the rich shall not give more than a half shekel, nor shall the poor give less.
Exo.30.15.kjv: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel, when they give an offering unto the Lord, to make an atonement for your souls.

Exo.23.3.bsb: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
Exo.23.3.kjv: Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.

Exo.23.6.bsb: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
Exo.23.6.kjv: Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause.

Exo.22.25.bsb: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
Exo.22.25.kjv: If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.

Exo.22.26.bsb: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
Exo.22.26.kjv: If thou at all take thy neighbour’s raiment to pledge, thou shalt deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down:

Exo.23.11.bsb: but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
Exo.23.11.kjv: But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.

Exo.14.15.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
Exo.14.15.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward:

Exo.14.16.bsb: And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
Exo.14.16.kjv: But lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thine hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the midst of the sea.

Exo.17.8.bsb: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
Exo.17.8.kjv: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

Exo.17.9.bsb: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”
Exo.17.9.kjv: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.

Exo.17.10.bsb: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
Exo.17.10.kjv: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

Exo.17.14.bsb: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
Exo.17.14.kjv: And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

Exo.3.10.bsb: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
Exo.3.10.kjv: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.

Exo.14.10.bsb: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them, and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
Exo.14.10.kjv: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the Lord.

Exo.14.11.bsb: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
Exo.14.11.kjv: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?

Exo.14.12.bsb: Did we not say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
Exo.14.12.kjv: Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.

Exo.14.14.bsb: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.”
Exo.14.14.kjv: The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

Exo.14.23.bsb: And the Egyptians chased after them—all Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen—and followed them into the sea.
Exo.14.23.kjv: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

Exo.33.16.bsb: For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us? How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?”
Exo.33.16.kjv: For wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth.

Exo.34.9.bsb: “O Lord,” he said, “if I have indeed found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”
Exo.34.9.kjv: And he said, If now I have found grace in thy sight, O Lord, let my Lord, I pray thee, go among us; for it is a stiffnecked people; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for thine inheritance.

Exo.9.16.bsb: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
Exo.9.16.kjv: And in very deed for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.

Exo.28.2.bsb: Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to give him glory and splendor.
Exo.28.2.kjv: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.

Exo.28.3.bsb: You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration, so that he may serve Me as priest.
Exo.28.3.kjv: And thou shalt speak unto all that are wise hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

Exo.29.44.bsb: So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
Exo.29.44.kjv: And I will sanctify the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar: I will sanctify also both Aaron and his sons, to minister to me in the priest’s office.

Exo.27.21.bsb: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.
Exo.27.21.kjv: In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.

Exo.28.43.bsb: Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.
Exo.28.43.kjv: And they shall be upon Aaron, and upon his sons, when they come in unto the tabernacle of the congregation, or when they come near unto the altar to minister in the holy place; that they bear not iniquity, and die: it shall be a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him.

Exo.29.1.bsb: “Now this is what you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
Exo.29.1.kjv: And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallow them, to minister unto me in the priest’s office: Take one young bullock, and two rams without blemish,

Exo.29.2.bsb: along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,
Exo.29.2.kjv: And unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of wheaten flour shalt thou make them.

Exo.29.3.bsb: put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Exo.29.3.kjv: And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, with the bullock and the two rams.

Exo.29.5.bsb: Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
Exo.29.5.kjv: And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him with the curious girdle of the ephod:

Exo.29.7.bsb: Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
Exo.29.7.kjv: Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.

Exo.29.8.bsb: Present his sons as well and clothe them with tunics.
Exo.29.8.kjv: And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.

Exo.29.19.bsb: Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
Exo.29.19.kjv: And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.

Exo.29.20.bsb: Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Splatter the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.
Exo.29.20.kjv: Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

Exo.29.21.bsb: And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.
Exo.29.21.kjv: And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be hallowed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.

Exo.29.23.bsb: along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Exo.29.23.kjv: And one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer out of the basket of the unleavened bread that is before the Lord:

Exo.29.24.bsb: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
Exo.29.24.kjv: And thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt wave them for a wave offering before the Lord.

Exo.29.25.bsb: Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is a food offering to the LORD.
Exo.29.25.kjv: And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the Lord: it is an offering made by fire unto the Lord.

Exo.29.26.bsb: Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
Exo.29.26.kjv: And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the Lord: and it shall be thy part.

Exo.29.27.bsb: Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
Exo.29.27.kjv: And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons:

Exo.29.28.bsb: This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites will make to the LORD from their peace offerings.
Exo.29.28.kjv: And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’ by a statute for ever from the children of Israel: for it is an heave offering: and it shall be an heave offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifice of their peace offerings, even their heave offering unto the Lord.

Exo.29.29.bsb: The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
Exo.29.29.kjv: And the holy garments of Aaron shall be his sons’ after him, to be anointed therein, and to be consecrated in them.

Exo.29.30.bsb: The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
Exo.29.30.kjv: And that son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days, when he cometh into the tabernacle of the congregation to minister in the holy place.

Exo.29.31.bsb: You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
Exo.29.31.kjv: And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seethe his flesh in the holy place.

Exo.29.32.bsb: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
Exo.29.32.kjv: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

Exo.29.33.bsb: They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.
Exo.29.33.kjv: And they shall eat those things wherewith the atonement was made, to consecrate and to sanctify them: but a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy.

Exo.29.34.bsb: And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.
Exo.29.34.kjv: And if ought of the flesh of the consecrations, or of the bread, remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the remainder with fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is holy.

Exo.29.35.bsb: This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.
Exo.29.35.kjv: And thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all things which I have commanded thee: seven days shalt thou consecrate them.

Exo.40.12.bsb: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Exo.40.12.kjv: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and wash them with water.

Exo.40.13.bsb: And you are to clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as a priest.
Exo.40.13.kjv: And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

Exo.40.14.bsb: Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
Exo.40.14.kjv: And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:

Exo.40.15.bsb: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may also serve Me as priests. Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.”
Exo.40.15.kjv: And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

Exo.40.16.bsb: Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
Exo.40.16.kjv: Thus did Moses: according to all that the Lord commanded him, so did he.

Exo.40.30.bsb: He placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing;
Exo.40.30.kjv: And he set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and put water there, to wash withal.

Exo.40.31.bsb: and from it Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet.
Exo.40.31.kjv: And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat:

Exo.40.32.bsb: They washed whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Exo.40.32.kjv: When they went into the tent of the congregation, and when they came near unto the altar, they washed; as the Lord commanded Moses.

Exo.28.5.bsb: They shall use gold, along with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
Exo.28.5.kjv: And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.

Exo.28.6.bsb: They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
Exo.28.6.kjv: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and of purple, of scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cunning work.

Exo.28.7.bsb: It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners, so it can be fastened.
Exo.28.7.kjv: It shall have the two shoulderpieces thereof joined at the two edges thereof; and so it shall be joined together.

Exo.28.8.bsb: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod must be of one piece, of the same workmanship—with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
Exo.28.8.kjv: And the curious girdle of the ephod, which is upon it, shall be of the same, according to the work thereof; even of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

Exo.28.9.bsb: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
Exo.28.9.kjv: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:

Exo.28.10.bsb: six of their names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth.
Exo.28.10.kjv: Six of their names on one stone, and the other six names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth.

Exo.28.11.bsb: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings.
Exo.28.11.kjv: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold.

Exo.28.12.bsb: Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD.
Exo.28.12.kjv: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulders of the ephod for stones of memorial unto the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord upon his two shoulders for a memorial.

Exo.28.13.kjv: And thou shalt make ouches of gold;

Exo.28.14.bsb: and two chains of pure gold, made of braided cord work; and attach these chains to the settings.
Exo.28.14.kjv: And two chains of pure gold at the ends; of wreathen work shalt thou make them, and fasten the wreathen chains to the ouches.

Exo.28.15.bsb: You are also to make a breastpiece of judgment with the same workmanship as the ephod. Construct it with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
Exo.28.15.kjv: And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work; after the work of the ephod thou shalt make it; of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.

Exo.28.16.bsb: It must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.
Exo.28.16.kjv: Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.

Exo.28.17.bsb: And mount on it a setting of gemstones, four rows of stones: In the first row there shall be a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald;
Exo.28.17.kjv: And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row.

Exo.28.18.bsb: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
Exo.28.18.kjv: And the second row shall be an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

Exo.28.19.bsb: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
Exo.28.19.kjv: And the third row a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.

Exo.28.20.bsb: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount these stones in gold filigree settings.
Exo.28.20.kjv: And the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings.

Exo.28.21.bsb: The twelve stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
Exo.28.21.kjv: And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.

Exo.28.22.bsb: For the breastpiece, make braided chains like cords of pure gold.
Exo.28.22.kjv: And thou shalt make upon the breastplate chains at the ends of wreathen work of pure gold.

Exo.28.23.bsb: You are also to make two gold rings and fasten them to the two corners of the breastpiece.
Exo.28.23.kjv: And thou shalt make upon the breastplate two rings of gold, and shalt put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.

Exo.28.24.bsb: Then fasten the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
Exo.28.24.kjv: And thou shalt put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings which are on the ends of the breastplate.

Exo.28.25.bsb: and fasten the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
Exo.28.25.kjv: And the other two ends of the two wreathen chains thou shalt fasten in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod before it.

Exo.28.26.bsb: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
Exo.28.26.kjv: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the two ends of the breastplate in the border thereof, which is in the side of the ephod inward.

Exo.28.27.bsb: Make two additional gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near its seam just above its woven waistband.
Exo.28.27.kjv: And two other rings of gold thou shalt make, and shalt put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart thereof, over against the other coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod.

Exo.28.28.bsb: The rings of the breastpiece shall be tied to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece is above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing out from the ephod.
Exo.28.28.kjv: And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.

Exo.28.30.bsb: And place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will also be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD.
Exo.28.30.kjv: And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goeth in before the Lord: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the Lord continually.

Exo.28.31.bsb: You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
Exo.28.31.kjv: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.

Exo.28.32.bsb: with an opening at its top in the center. Around the opening shall be a woven collar with an opening like that of a garment, so that it will not tear.
Exo.28.32.kjv: And there shall be an hole in the top of it, in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of woven work round about the hole of it, as it were the hole of an habergeon, that it be not rent.

Exo.28.33.bsb: Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all the way around the lower hem, with gold bells between them,
Exo.28.33.kjv: And beneath upon the hem of it thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, round about the hem thereof; and bells of gold between them round about:

Exo.28.34.bsb: alternating the gold bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe.
Exo.28.34.kjv: A golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe round about.

Exo.28.35.bsb: Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he will not die.
Exo.28.35.kjv: And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and his sound shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place before the Lord, and when he cometh out, that he die not.

Exo.28.41.bsb: After you put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests.
Exo.28.41.kjv: And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him; and shalt anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

Exo.28.42.bsb: Make linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, extending from waist to thigh.
Exo.28.42.kjv: And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:
